text: Add to Peano Arithmetic a new constant c together with the infinitely many axioms c ≠ 0̄, c ≠ 1̄, c ≠ 2̄, …. What does the Compactness Theorem let us conclude about this extended theory?
choices: It is satisfiable, so PA has a non-standard model containing an element greater than every standard numeral
It is unsatisfiable, because c cannot differ from every numeral
Its only model is the standard model ℕ
explanation: Every finite subset uses only finitely many axioms c ≠ n̄, and is satisfied by ℕ interpreting c as a large enough number; by compactness the whole theory has a model — a non-standard model of PA with an 'infinite' element. Options B and C are wrong precisely because finite satisfiability holds; option D contradicts the existence of the new element c that differs from all numerals.
